what: Every model and analysis on one page: score on data it did not learn from, the simple baseline, and whether it met the pass rule written before it ran.
note: Scores are copied from each model's own output file by scripts/build_trust.py.

rows.name: Will a droplet flame go out?
rows.tested: Whole test sessions held out: 5-fold grouped by ISS test date (80 dates), repeated 20 times. Score = median AUC; range = 95% session bootstrap.
rows.rule: Median AUC at least 0.80 and range above the one-variable baseline (models/m7-extinction/RULES.md, R1)

rows.name: How fast does a droplet burn?
rows.tested: Whole test sessions held out: 5-fold grouped by ISS test date (80 dates), repeated 20 times. Score = median MAE; range = 95% session bootstrap.
rows.rule: Beats the d-squared law and the per-fuel mean in 16 of 20 repeats (R2)

rows.name: Does a cool flame keep burning?
rows.tested: Whole test sessions held out: 5-fold grouped by ISS test date (39 dates), repeated 20 times. Score = median AUC; range = 95% session bootstrap.
rows.rule: Lower end of the AUC range above 0.5 (R3). Note: its range overlaps a pressure-only rule.

rows.name: Will the detector miss this smoke?
rows.baseline: Material only (logistic, leave one test out)
rows.tested: leave one flight test out (16 folds); ranges from 2,000 bootstrap resamples

rows.name: How fast does flame cross an acrylic slab? (M6)
rows.metric: R² (held-out sessions, spread rate in mm/s)
rows.baseline: Training-set mean, no physics (added after audit)
rows.tested: Whole ISS sessions held out: leave one session out (7 sessions, grouped by GMT day). Score = R2 on the pooled held-out predictions; range = 95% session bootstrap. Holding out single tests instead gives R2 -0.77.
rows.caveat: Loses to simply predicting the average spread rate.

rows.name: Will it spread, and how fast? (M6b)
rows.metric: Mean error on held-out sessions, mm/s; range coverage
rows.baseline: Lookup by thickness and sides burning, no physics (added after audit)
rows.caveat: Meets its own rules, but a no-physics lookup is about as accurate on these 39 slabs.
rows.tested: Whole ISS sessions held out; two independent Saffire-II rates

rows.name: Where does the smoke go?
rows.tested: Tuned on Sample 1 burn (flame seen by radiometers 61 to 410 s after T0); tested on Smoke-wire puff (wire on 32 to 44 s)
rows.rule: The held-out smoke puff should match too (shown on the smoke model's check figure)

rows.name: Would a fast-rise alarm be quicker?
rows.metric: Events where it beat the fixed alarm
rows.tested: All three Saffire-III events, each on its own
rows.rule: Earlier in 2 of 3 events and no false alarms (models/m4-latency/RULES.md)
